title: Integer division by zero
verdict: no finding (`verify`: division by zero error)
description: Native, under `error_on_division_by_zero = true`, the 2.0 default. With the setting off, DuckDB returns NULL, so it needs a guard, `CASE WHEN y = 0 THEN error('division by zero') ELSE x // y END`. A plan that asks for `NULL` needs `CASE WHEN y = 0 THEN NULL ELSE x // y END`.
Truncation is native: `-7 // 2 = -3`, in every agreeing entry and fuzz case.
reference: Substrait and the reference: `divide` on integers truncates toward zero; with `on_division_by_zero` omitted, a zero divisor raises.

Lean: no finding. `verify` reports `division by zero` as an error, so on those rows the plan may raise, which is the reference. `Rel.eval`'s NULL there ([`Expr.lean:195`](../../SubstraitLean/Expr.lean#L195)) is not an answer anyone sees. It is the reference value for `NULL`, should a plan ask for it.

provenance.notes: `on_division_by_zero: ERROR` matches; `NULL` with `error_on_division_by_zero` off. `sverify_dev.probe` runs the function at each signature on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the 64-bit bounds, 0.5, ±2.5, 1e308, ±inf, NaN, NULL), one row at a time from columns, under every combination of `error_on_division_by_zero` and `ieee_floating_point_ops`. Lean evaluates the Substrait call on the same rows once per candidate value of its option (`substrait-check --outcomes`), and the candidates whose outcomes all match are DuckDB's options. No input is -0.0 (duckdb-R14).
